summary: Aaron Fuks of Hyros (Denver) explains how he built a B2B referral-pipeline business for home service trades (siding, painting, electrical, landscaping). He cold calls and mass-texts businesses in adjacent trades, gets a real bid or project first, then uses it as proof to sell partner introductions to a client. Pricing moved from $150 per appointment to $6,000 for 10 intros plus a $250-500/month nurturing fee, with claimed revenue around $27K last month. Key takeaway: bring value first (a real bid), sell relationships rather than leads, and run it on GoHighLevel with minimal cost.

speakers.name: Aaron Fuks
speakers.description: Founder of Hyros, referral pipelines for home service businesses, Denver

ideas.name: Referral pipeline / partner-introduction service for home service trades
ideas.one_liner: Cold call and text adjacent-trade businesses to find live bids, then sell tradespeople bundles of vetted referral partner introductions plus ongoing relationship nurturing.
ideas.business_model: Per-appointment fee, then packaged intros (10 for $6,000) plus monthly nurturing/management subscription
ideas.customer: Home service business owners (siding, painting, electrical, landscaping, interior design, general contractors) wanting referral partners in adjacent trades
ideas.problem: Trades want steady high-value jobs from upstream partners (roofers, builders, designers) but lead marketplaces are shared and poor quality, and cold outreach is hard and time-consuming.
ideas.offer: Introductions to referral partners who have live bids, guarantee of two real bids in the first 20 appointments, replacement partners if no quote is delivered in time, plus CRM-based relationship nurturing and storm/blast text automations.

pricing.model: Package of intros plus monthly management fee (originally per appointment)
pricing.notes: Pricing 4x'd after pivot to packages with guarantees. Close is a menu: 20, 40 or 120 appointments. Commission of ~30% paid to the caller per appointment.

acquisition_channels.details: Early on: Google Maps lists, 20-40 dials a day with a GoHighLevel power dialer, 15 second ring time, no voicemails, custom dispositions; roughly 2 appointments per day. Also calls immediately when someone replies to a text.

quote.text: we're using go high level. It has a built-in like power dialer thing.
quote.speaker: Aaron Fuks

acquisition_channels.details: Mass text a few hundred partner businesses (e.g. 200 custom builders and luxury remodelers) asking if they have projects needing a specialist bid; 2-5% reply with a project; then text prospective clients saying a bid is available (10-15% response) and call replies immediately. Texts drip out to keep call volume manageable.

quote.text: we pulled a huge list of all the roofers in our area and we sent a text to every single one of them
quote.speaker: Aaron Fuks

acquisition_channels.details: Offers it white-label or via partnership to marketing agencies, who sell it to their own clients.
Website hyros.com with a referral pipeline blueprint PDF used as sales collateral.

ideas.delivery: Aaron's team sources partner businesses with live bids via calls and texts, qualifies them by phone, books appointments with the client, then manages relationships and referral tracking through GoHighLevel automations. One commission-only caller helps with calls.
unit_economics_claims: About 90% profit, one commission-only caller taking ~30% per appointment
Painting client got 4 bids worth $17K-$64K within 48 hours, paid for about 3 years of nurturing fees
Revenue about $27K last month, up from $14K in June
ideas.startup_cost: Low: a few hundred dollars a month of software and texting
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Immediate; began earning per appointment within the first month of calling

acquisition.how: Texting and CRM drips are automatable, but UK PECR bars unsolicited texts to sole traders and many trades are sole traders; the human phone call to qualify and close is central. Cold email to limited companies and call screening against TPS/CTPS are lawful alternatives.

onboarding.how: Client onboarding is a sales call plus PDF blueprint and GoHighLevel sub-account setup; agents could handle the setup but closing relies on a human.

delivery.how: Qualifying partners and verifying bids needs human phone conversations; nurturing sequences and referral tracking are automated.

billing.how: Packages and monthly fees can be billed through Stripe or GoHighLevel invoicing with little oversight.

support.how: Weekly check-in calls and appointment follow-ups; automations and agents can handle most updates.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in principle with UK trades (roofers, builders, electricians). Texting sole traders without consent breaches PECR; the speaker relies on lax US business-text rules. Use cold email to limited companies, TPS/CTPS-screened calls, and Companies House data. Insurance-claim siding jobs are US-specific.

risks: TCPA/PECR legal exposure for cold texting
Depends on the client's close rate and on bids converting
Gatekeepers and project managers lack the incentive to refer
Perceived as a scam or lead-gen company
Needs a continuing supply of fresh partners and bids
Clients get busy and stop buying more intros

tactics.name: Bring a real bid first, then sell the relationship
steps: Text a list of partner businesses (e.g. roofers, builders) asking if they have projects needing your trade
Call every positive reply immediately to qualify the bid
Text prospective client businesses saying you have a live bid and want to partner
Call replies at once and pitch partner introductions as relationships, not leads

quote.text: Bring them a project and then they believe in the value.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Cold call setup in GoHighLevel
steps: Do not leave voicemails; retry later
Add custom dispositions (picked up, pitched, angry) to track

tactics.name: Upgrade from per-appointment to guaranteed package
steps: Start low per appointment to learn close rates
Guarantee two real bids in the first 20 appointments
Replace partners that fail to deliver a quote in time

tactics.name: Commission-only caller
steps: Pay a caller roughly 30% of each appointment fee

tools_mentioned.name: GoHighLevel
tools_mentioned.purpose: CRM, power dialer, SMS automation, snapshots and sub-accounts
tools_mentioned.cost_stated: a couple hundred dollars a month

warnings.warning: Gatekeepers and project managers are not incentivised, so follow-up calls to them close poorly; target owners.

quote.text: With project manager, he's probably going to make the same whether you make this connection or not
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Prospects often think it is a scam or lead gen company; frame as relationship partnership.
Cold text laws (TCPA in the US) are looser for B2B but still a risk; UK PECR is stricter for sole traders.

lessons.lesson: Prove value before asking for money: bringing a live bid first earns trust and attention.
Start with a low price to learn close rates, then raise sharply once you see client demand for volume.

quote.text: I think it is smart to price it low to start because his close rate could be 2%, it could be 20%
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Aim for 10x-1000x ROI for the customer, not 2-3x.
Cold outreach is only as hard as your offer.

quote.text: cold calling is hard, but it's only as hard as your offer.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Sell the relationship, not the lead; this differentiates from shared-lead marketplaces.
Add recurring revenue (nurturing) to a one-off service so success doesn't put you out of business.
Pick a niche you are excited about rather than the shiniest object on the platform.
Work with an existing client, observe the value chain and spot the upstream/downstream opportunity.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with consistent process detail and numbers, but revenue is unverified and figures are somewhat vague (recurring vs one-off confusion); small sample of client stories.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host receives affiliate kickback from GoHighLevel; guest sells services and a blueprint via Hyros and seeks agency partners.
